summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge by analyzing Soony's confidential launch data, then building a general, adaptable product that detects contradictions, acts on them (supplier emails, approvals) and handles new data drops.
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's plan hid Collector's Edition shortfalls (overbooked art books, failed statues, stale counts) and built a deployed polling + extraction + recheck + act app with Today/Launch views, routines, an approval loop, a README, and a dry-mode demo instance; most work is committed and pushed, with the hand-in (demo script, video, pitch) still pending.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (list files, get file, archive.zip) and no webhooks or notifications; the documented approach is polling the file list and comparing SHA-256 checksums, because files are replaced under the same name.
Confidential data lives in the gitignored data/ folder; .env holds the portal token and is gitignored, while .env.example is committed.
The team uses CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md for workflow and task claiming; work lives on branch jonas/today-flow and Entire writes checkpoints only when repo files change.
Prepared routine proposals can go stale when their case is decided elsewhere, so they must expire automatically and be deduped across routines.

Internal messages and escalations were only recorded, not delivered, until the sign-off loop (signoff.py, /ok/<token> page) added push/Teams delivery; push goes to every subscribed device, not one person.
ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK is empty in .env so Teams delivery is not active; ASK_SIGNOFF_SIMULATE=<seconds> enables a labelled simulated approval for demos.
A demo instance with dry mail mode (no real supplier emails, resettable) runs on its own hostname via the Cloudflare tunnel.

code.finding: New module implementing one-time approval links, push delivery, approve/decline and simulated approval; basic_auth.py lets valid /ok tokens bypass the dashboard password.
Left list selection bug: opening a decided case also marked the first Needs-you case as selected, causing scroll jumps; fixed by not marking Needs-you rows while a decided case is open.
Routine diagram rendered as n8n-style nodes (When, one Only-if node, Then steps) on a dotted canvas.

workflow: Subagents are effective for large cross-checks (200 order confirmations and 59 scans) and for parallel builder tasks while the main session writes docs.
Verify UI fixes in a real browser with screenshots and scroll measurements rather than trusting the type check.
Shared mailbox sync wrote a stale copy of the action log back and lost records; appending under a shared lock plus a test fixed it, so check for lost-update races in sync jobs.
Use a dry-mode second instance for demos so rehearsals don't email real suppliers.
Confirm before pushing or sending outward-facing emails; commit work in small steps with tests (320 tests passing).
